chunks: Al-Ḥalabī asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the qunūt.
Is there a specific wording in it? So he said: “Praise your Lord, send blessings upon your Prophet, and seek forgiveness for your sin.”

key_terms.الْقُنُوتِ: the supplication recited in the standing posture of salat (prayer)
key_terms.قَوْلٌ: a verbal formula or wording to be said
key_terms.نَبِيِّكَ: your Prophet, upon whom blessings are invoked

ai.seo_question: What should be said in the qunūt during salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith states a concise formula for qunūt in salat (prayer): praising Allah, sending blessings upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and seeking forgiveness. It indicates that qunūt may be fulfilled through remembrance, salawat, and istighfar in a simple and known form.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.933 - Al-Halabi asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) about what should be said in the Qunoot (the supplication during prayer).
Imam (as) replied: "Praise your Lord (azj), send blessings upon your Prophet, and seek forgiveness for your sins."
